# Marble Skill Taxonomy

An open, structured taxonomy of **what children learn** across the primary/elementary years — decomposed into fine-grained "micro-topics", wired into a prerequisite graph, and aligned to national curriculum standards. Produced by [Marble](https://withmarble.com).

> **Version:** `v1` · **Topics:** 1,861 · **Prerequisite edges:** 4,003 · **Subjects:** 9

## See it



Every dot is a micro-topic, colored by subject; height is age; each thread is a prerequisite ([full-quality video](media/curriculum-viz.mp4)). Explore it interactively at [withmarble.com/curriculum](https://withmarble.com/curriculum) — tap any concept to trace everything a learner must master before it.


## What this is

Most curriculum data is either a flat list of standards or locked inside a product. This dataset is a **connected graph of learning**:

- **1,861 micro-topics** — a single, teachable idea (e.g. *"Building sentences"*, *"Apparent brightness of stars"*), each with a plain-language description, mastery **evidence** criteria, a type (conceptual / procedural / representational / language / meta), a subject + domain, and an approximate age range.
- **4,003 prerequisite dependencies** — a directed acyclic graph: *"topic X depends on prerequisite Y"*, each edge tagged `hard`/`soft` and carrying a one-line **reason**.
- **Curriculum alignment** — each micro-topic links to the standards it was distilled from (NGSS, Common Core, the UK National Curriculum, and more).
- **Teaching research** — 1,049 records. Coverage is partial; 812 topics have no research in this release.
- **Domain clusters** — 176 parent-friendly one-paragraph summaries per (subject, domain, age band).

### Subjects

| Subject | Topics |
|---|---:|
| Computing | 52 |
| English | 339 |
| Geography | 22 |
| History | 109 |
| Learning to Learn | 18 |
| Life Skills | 46 |
| Mathematics | 581 |
| Personal & Social Development | 118 |
| Science | 576 |

## Files

All data lives in [`data/`](data/) as UTF-8 JSON. See [`schema/`](schema/) for JSON Schemas and [`manifest.json`](data/manifest.json) for counts + SHA-256 checksums.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [`data/topics.json`](data/topics.json) | The micro-topics (graph **nodes**). |
| [`data/dependencies.json`](data/dependencies.json) | Prerequisite **edges** (`topicId` depends on `prerequisiteId`). |
| [`data/curriculum-standards.json`](data/curriculum-standards.json) | The source curriculum standards, grouped by curriculum. |
| [`data/clusters.json`](data/clusters.json) | Parent-friendly domain summaries. |
| [`data/teaching-research.json`](data/teaching-research.json) | Teaching research joined by `topicId`, with explicit coverage and publication notes (~24 MB). |
| [`data/archived-teaching-research.json`](data/archived-teaching-research.json) | Historical guidance for merged or refocused topics, with original records and current topic associations. |
| [`data/manifest.json`](data/manifest.json) | Counts, per-subject breakdown, per-file checksums. |
| [`data/curriculum-alignments.json`](data/curriculum-alignments.json) | Scoped framework, jurisdiction and global age contexts; source for flat compatibility fields. |

The catalogue contains **19 sources / 8,313 standards/source-position records**. A separate [NCERT NCF-SE October 2024 edition proposal](reports/ncert-ncfse-preparatory-core-catalogue-2026-11-09.md) contributes 254 formal stage goals/competencies: 172 Preparatory records shared across Grades 3–5 and [82 Foundational records](reports/ncert-ncfse-foundational-catalogue-2026-11-09.md) preserving full ages 3–8 stage scope, without grade clones; the [Arts/PE extension](reports/ncert-ncfse-preparatory-arts-pe-catalogue-2026-11-09.md) preserves nested source-set applicability. The NCERT foundational source contributes 316 positions: 67 Maths, 34 English L2, 66 Physical/Motor, 34 Socio-emotional/Ethical, 30 Arts, 18 Learning Habits and 11 Cognitive positions intersecting Grades 1–2, plus 56 shared-stage positions from the [Arts syllabus explicit outcome column](reports/ncert-foundational-arts-syllabus-catalogue-2026-11-09.md) without an invented required grade. Shared grade cells and a repeated printed English requirement are preserved; source-position totals count neither distinct skills nor grade memberships. See the [NCERT catalogue report](reports/ncert-english-l2-catalogue-2026-11-09.md) and [remaining primary scope](reports/ncert-primary-catalogue-scope-2026-11-09.md). It includes 620 Australian Curriculum v9 content descriptions and 3,862 Ontario expectations from nine elementary documents. Ontario is exported as codes and official source links only; ingestion of source expectations is separate from authoring topic coverage. Ontario Grades 1–7 Mathematics have received focused taxonomy authoring passes. The [Grade 2 report](reports/ontario-grade2-mathematics-2026-10-23.md) distinguishes reused claims, extracted elementary claims and the concurrency gap; mappings do not certify learner mastery of every linked topic. The [Grade 3 report](reports/ontario-grade3-mathematics-2026-10-23.md) records reuse of 114 existing topics, the congruence extension and prerequisite repairs; no topics were added. The [Grade 4 report](reports/ontario-grade4-mathematics-2026-10-24.md) records reuse of 126 existing topics, two missing skills, two focused extractions and prerequisite repairs. The [Grade 5 report](reports/ontario-grade5-mathematics-2026-10-24.md) records reuse of 145 existing topics, one missing mathematical representation, one financial/civic concept and one focused extraction. The [Grade 6 report](reports/ontario-grade6-mathematics-2026-10-27.md) records reuse of 173 existing topics and five additions: two procedures, one focused extraction and two financial-content claims. The [Grade 7 report](reports/ontario-grade7-mathematics-2026-10-27.md) records reuse of 171 existing topics and two spatial additions; the square-root proposal was withdrawn.

The NCERT primary alignment stack has proposed review dispositions for [all 570 accepted source keys](reports/ncert-alignment-readiness-2026-11-10.json). The [final Preparatory TWAU slice](reports/ncert-twau-alignment-2026-11-10.md) reviews 32 records through reuse, completing source-position review after the Maths, language, observation, physical, learning-habit, socio-emotional and Arts slices. Formal stage requirements and suggestive positions remain distinct. Reviewed does not mean all Full, accepted, published or learner attainment: language/art-form bindings, contextual requirements and one unresolved physical musical-scale phrase remain explicit. The [first Foundational Maths report](reports/ncert-foundational-mathematics-alignment-2026-11-10.md) retains its initial historical dispositions; later source-fit protocols resolve most performance conditions without country, grade or difficulty clones. Default-branch reconciliation and downstream compatibility remain separate.

Ontario Grade 5 Language adds 306 links across 161 existing topics, with no new topics. The [Grade 5 Language report](reports/ontario-grade5-language-2026-11-02.md) and [code-by-code mapping](reports/ontario-grade5-language-mapping-2026-11-02.json) record whole-topic reuse, prerequisite repairs, and the four remaining resource/performance conditions. Coverage links do not certify learner mastery.

Ontario Grade 6 Language adds 313 links across 168 topics, including three new claims and a suffix-evidence correction. The [Grade 6 Language report](reports/ontario-grade6-language-2026-11-02.md) and [code-by-code mapping](reports/ontario-grade6-language-mapping-2026-11-02.json) record 55 Full / 4 Partial specific expectations, with resource and performance conditions retained. This Language pass stops at primary Grade 6 (ages 11–12).

The Australian cleanup reviewed all 314 additions and 14 later edited IDs, consolidated repeated skills and redistributed bundled requirements. All 593 selected expectation codes remain linked. Those links do not certify whole-standard coverage: 572 previous Full claims have not been independently recertified. The 27 PE/movement descriptions remain excluded. Read the [cleanup report](reports/acara-v9-cleanup-2026-10-23.md) and [current area-by-area mapping counts](reports/acara-v9-scope-coverage.md).

See [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) for sources and attribution.

The [Ontario primary status inventory](reports/ontario-primary-status-2026-11-09.md)
separates catalogue ingestion, recorded associations and historical coverage
reviews by subject and grade. The [Grade 1 Science review](reports/ontario-grade1-science-2026-11-09.md)
accounts for all 55 selected codes, proposing existing-topic associations while
retaining coverage conditions and focused decisions for follow-up.
The [Grade 2 Science review](reports/ontario-grade2-science-2026-11-09.md)
accounts for all 52 selected codes using existing claims, with unresolved
source/assessment conditions made explicit.
The [Grade 3 Science review](reports/ontario-grade3-science-2026-11-09.md)
records all 55 codes, existing-topic reuse and verified Ontario soil examples,
with remaining conditions explicit.

Ontario Grade 4 Science has a [code-by-code review](reports/ontario-grade4-science-2026-11-09.md)
covering all retained codes with existing-topic reuse and explicit remaining conditions.

Ontario Grade 5 Science has a [code-by-code review](reports/ontario-grade5-science-2026-11-09.md)
covering all retained codes with existing-topic reuse and explicit remaining conditions.

Ontario Grade 6 Science has a [code-by-code review](reports/ontario-grade6-science-2026-11-09.md)
covering all retained codes; primary Science review has explicit dispositions through Grade 6.

These grade reports retain their historical authoring bases. The current
integration delivers their reviewed changes together after Grade 1 reached main.

The [cross-grade Science residual review](reports/ontario-primary-science-residual-review-2026-11-09.md)
groups remaining conditions across all primary grades without treating Partial judgments as new topics.

### Adding curricula

For human-readable curation decisions, see the
[curation principles](docs/curation/principles.md),
[ingestion and alignment guidelines](docs/curation/alignment-guidelines.md) and
[reviewed examples](docs/curation/reviewed-examples.md). Agents can use the
[taxonomy-curation skill](.agents/skills/taxonomy-curation/SKILL.md), for example:
`Use $taxonomy-curation to audit the remaining primary-school Ontario alignments.`
The skill is optional; contributors submit the actual change in an ordinary PR
and need no private account. Hosted builders must explicitly load these versioned

Generation refreshes flat topic standards/ages, the research file's topic checksum binding and manifest checksums/counts. It uses only public local files and preserves original timestamps; no private account is needed. Authored research and its coverage must already be valid; this bounded command does not author research or repair unrelated artifacts.

The authoring and publication design describes downstream application deployment. This public baseline does not apply changes to a live DB, migrate agent tools or activate the future publisher.

Curricula map onto one shared taxonomy. Keep subjects and domains consistent across countries; a curriculum's learning-area labels do not create separate subject trees.

  • Reuse a topic when it assesses the same concept or operation. Add local examples without changing what mastery means.
  • Review affected assessment guidance and learner estimates before changing a mastery claim. Assess independent procedures separately; topics do not track multiple difficulty levels.
  • Record whole-expectation, component and prerequisite contributions explicitly. A topic–code link alone does not establish Full coverage.
  • Reuse existing domains before adding a distinct new domain. Keep names consistent and avoid parallel country-specific domain trees.
  • Keep each topic focused on a teachable concept or skill. A standard can link to several topics; its bundled requirements need not become one topic.
  • Add country-specific topics where the knowledge genuinely differs, such as a country's history or constitutional arrangements. Use shared topics for common concepts and skills, with local examples where useful.

A topic

{
  "id": "mt_N8CpN1EJrP",
  "type": "CONCEPTUAL",
  "subject": "English",
  "domain": "Grammar & Punctuation",
  "name": "Building sentences",
  "description": "Understand that words combine to make sentences — a sentence expresses a complete thought…",
  "ageRangeStart": 4,
  "ageRangeEnd": 6,
  "centrality": 0.257,
  "evidence": [
    "Distinguish between complete sentences and fragments",
    "Compose a complete sentence with a subject and verb"
  ],
  "assessmentPrompt": "If {{name}} says something like \"The dog\", can they tell you that's not a complete sentence…?",
  "standards": ["ccss-ela:L.K.1f", "uk-nc-2013:Eng.App2.Y1.Sent.1"]
}
  • id — stable identifier (mt_…), referenced by dependencies and by neighbours.
  • standards — keys into curriculum-standards.json ("<curriculum-slug>:<code>").
  • assessmentPrompt — a natural-language check for the idea. Contains a {{name}} placeholder (the child's name); substitute or strip before display.

A dependency

{ "topicId": "mt__00ZSLnB7p", "prerequisiteId": "mt_VBl1T1sFCM", "strength": "hard",
  "reason": "Must understand vibrations make sound before finding volume patterns" }

topicId depends on prerequisiteId. Reverse the edge to get "unlocks".

Teaching research

data/teaching-research.json adds how a topic might be taught to the graph of what children learn. It contains 1,049 active topic records. coverage.missingTopicIds and per-subject counts make the 809 topics without research explicit; absence is not a judgement about whether a topic can be taught.

archived-teaching-research.json preserves two historical records excluded from active coverage after a topic merge and a change in learning scope. Each entry includes the original topic and research record, its archive reason, and related current topic IDs. The archive also records the assessment prerequisite reference redirected after the merge.

The active teaching-research.json file has schemaVersion: 1 and taxonomy version: "v1". Each records[] entry joins topics.json through topicId and contains:

Field Meaning
pedagogy Original teaching summary, practices, representations and misconceptions.
learn Portable learning guidance (schemaVersion: 2): a summary, activities, educational constraints and review notes.
learn.activities[] Learner actions, intended insight, feedback, rationale and supporting source claims. No product artifact types or fit rankings.
assess Original diagnostic/task, response levels, error patterns and next teaching moves; nullable in the public interface.
sources Claim, named source, optional URL and the original author's verification flag.
confidence Original authoring confidence; not an independent quality score.
provenance Original authoring model and source record timestamps. The update timestamp also reflects the learning-guidance rewrite.
publicationNotes Paths and curriculum codes for text omitted under the codes-only publication policy.

sourceClaims exactly match sources[].claim after publication transformations. A source may support a general principle or curriculum alignment; this does not mean the proposed activity was tested. Some activities have no directly linked source claim.

These records were agent-authored. The learning guidance was rewritten for portability, checked by a separate factual critic, and sampled by a second agent. Most original pedagogy and assessment were retained and may contain claims that the updated guidance qualifies; chart-specific alignment repairs after #30 are recorded in the affected learning-guidance review notes; read the constraints and review notes alongside them. Sources were not re-fetched or re-verified for the initial publication; later nutrition-guide checks are recorded in the affected review notes. Historical verified: true and confidence: "high" are not new evidence ratings. Activities are research-informed proposals, not empirically validated interventions.

Nutrition terminology corrections in #63 update the existing Animal Nutrition, Balanced Diet & Food Groups, and Nutrients in a Healthy Diet guidance, activities and assessment to distinguish nutrients from food groups. Balanced-plate activities use food groups in a local guide; the records retain their identities. See the review note.

Some original research quoted restricted curriculum standards. Matched passages are replaced with inline curriculum references, including inside citation claims; all transformed paths are listed in publicationNotes. This is a conservative mechanical omission pass, not comprehensive rights clearance. Consult the linked upstream sources for their wording and terms. See PROVENANCE.md.

After the chart split in #30, mt_bESTSBB0wK covers pie charts, mt_H6LlpWgEYS covers earlier line-graph problem-solving, and mt_HlNSurPVDp has a separate construction-and-interpretation record. The new record adapts existing graph research; it is not a fresh literature review, and all reused source-verification flags are false. Its assessment requires a complete constructed graph. The later grouped-charts assessment routes graph-choice errors to data presentation and sector-angle errors to pie charts.

The file is bound to the exact topics.json bytes through topicFileSha256. Regenerate the research projection when the canonical topic file changes, even when topic IDs remain stable.

Using it

Pure data — no runtime, no dependencies. Load the JSON and go.

import topics from './data/topics.json' with { type: 'json' };
import deps from './data/dependencies.json' with { type: 'json' };

const byId = new Map(topics.topics.map(t => [t.id, t]));
const prereqs = deps.dependencies
  .filter(d => d.topicId === 'mt_N8CpN1EJrP')
  .map(d => byId.get(d.prerequisiteId).name);

Join teaching guidance to a topic:

import research from './data/teaching-research.json' with { type: 'json' };

const guidanceByTopic = new Map(research.records.map(r => [r.topicId, r]));
const guidance = guidanceByTopic.get('mt_N8CpN1EJrP'); // undefined: English is not covered yet
const activities = guidance?.learn.activities ?? [];

Validate structure, research coverage, evidence links and checksums:

node scripts/validate.mjs
node --test scripts/teaching-research.test.mjs

Marble Builder

The marble-builder agent skill helps turn a child's age and a user-confirmed goal into a standalone HTML learning experience that works offline by default. It uses topic prerequisites and available teaching research, develops a targeted research brief when needed, and agrees a concept with you before building. Experiences use visual interactions, scaffolding, UI-assessed transfer tasks and optional extensions. Spatial topics use Three.js with direct scene manipulation and a crafted cel-shaded look with flat colors and black outlines. Visual simulations must meet a beauty, craft and polish bar as well as work correctly. The public skill includes Marble-derived UI tokens, tactile controls refined in Moon Visit and Sky Colour Explorer, and the openly licensed Baloo 2 font, with one title and one instruction visible at a time: a small top-left title and a large, prominent instruction or explanation, plus concise button labels paired with icons. Water Lab is the visual quality reference. The agent renders, inspects and iterates in the browser rather than stopping at the first working HTML file.

The skill includes five runnable examples with readable source, key-state screenshots and design notes: Moon Visit, Sky Colour Explorer, Hidden Cubes, Bee Builder and Otter Forest. The notes explain what to borrow and where each prototype has limits or exceptions.

Optional connected LLM mode requires explicit author approval and a learning goal whose open-ended reasoning or text production cannot be adequately supported locally. That mode requires internet and a separate account connection; ChatGPT plan usage is a preview option for eligible local/open-source integrations.

In Codex, open this repository and invoke $marble-builder, for example:

Use $marble-builder to help my 8-year-old understand why equivalent fractions represent the same quantity.

Other agents can follow the linked SKILL.md directly. No Marble account or hosting is required. New reusable teaching research can optionally be proposed as a separate PR, with no child-specific information included.

License

This dataset is multi-licensed — read this before you use or redistribute it.

Layer License
The database — the collection, structure, IDs, topic↔topic and topic↔standard relationships ODbL 1.0 — free for research and commercial use, attribution required, share-alike (derivative databases must stay open under ODbL).
The textual content Marble authored — topic description/name/evidence/assessmentPrompt, dependency reasons, cluster summarys, original teaching-research prose CC BY-SA 4.0 — same spirit: attribution + share-alike.
Marble-authored learning examples — application source, original artwork, captures and design notes CC BY-SA 4.0. Bundled Three.js and Baloo 2 retain their separate MIT and OFL licenses and notices.
curriculum-standards.json — extracted from third-party frameworks Not Marble's to relicense. Each source is under its own upstream license — see PROVENANCE.md.

Why share-alike + still commercial-friendly: ODbL distinguishes a derivative database (extend/modify the taxonomy → must stay open) from a produced work (use it inside a product, model, or app → stays yours). So you can build a commercial product on this without open-sourcing your product; you only owe back improvements to the taxonomy itself.

Attribution

Any use must credit:

Marble Skill Taxonomy (v1) · © Generative Spark, Inc. (Marble) · https://withmarble.com · licensed under ODbL 1.0 (database) and CC BY-SA 4.0 (content).

Plus the upstream notices in PROVENANCE.md for any curriculum standards you use. See CITATION.cff for a formal citation.

What's not here

Deliberately excluded from this release: semantic embeddings (derived, recomputable) and any per-child / user data (never published). See CHANGELOG.md.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open, graph-based taxonomy mapping primary education skills and prerequisites for curriculum development.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Marble Skill Taxonomy is an open-source, structured dataset that decomposes primary and elementary education into a connected graph of learning. Instead of providing a flat list of standards, it breaks down education into 1,590 fine-grained micro-topics, each wired together by over 3,200 prerequisite dependencies. Each topic includes mastery criteria, plain-language descriptions, and direct alignments to national curriculum standards like Common Core and NGSS. This directed acyclic graph allows educators and developers to programmatically trace the exact learning path a student must master before grasping complex concepts.
keyFeatures: Micro-topic decomposition: Breaks down general subjects into 1,590 highly specific, teachable ideas with clear mastery criteria.
Prerequisite mapping: Connects topics using a directed acyclic graph to explicitly define the required learning path.
Standard alignment: Maps every micro-topic directly to established national curricula like Common Core and the UK National Curriculum.
Interactive visualization: Provides a comprehensive visual map allowing users to explore subjects and trace prerequisites interactively.
Structured data format: Delivers the entire curriculum graph as structured data, making it easy to integrate into educational software.

useCases.title: EdTech curriculum development
useCases.description: Software developers use the graph data to build adaptive learning platforms that intelligently suggest the next topic for a student.

useCases.title: Lesson planning
useCases.description: Teachers consult the prerequisite map to ensure they cover all necessary foundational skills before introducing a complex subject.

useCases.title: Curriculum alignment auditing
useCases.description: Administrators utilize the taxonomy to verify that their school's syllabus correctly aligns with required national standards.

useCases.title: Educational research
useCases.description: Researchers analyze the graph structure to identify learning bottlenecks and optimize the sequencing of educational materials.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This dataset is built for EdTech developers, curriculum designers, and educational researchers looking to build adaptive learning systems or analyze educational pathways. It requires familiarity with JSON or graph data structures to implement programmatically.
